metas.name: Hoop Dreams
metas.description:
The American dream appears here as a system that uses kids up. Two Chicago teenagers filmed over five years chasing basketball as a way out, as school, family, money and injury keep intervening.

A film following the lives of two inner-city Chicago boys who struggle to become college basketball players on the road to going professional.

metas.name: Paris Is Burning
metas.description:
Inside exclusion, people invent family, language and glamour. New York ball culture — houses as chosen families, categories, voguing — joyful and blunt about race, poverty and murder.

A chronicle of New York's drag scene in the 1980s, focusing on balls, voguing and the ambitions and dreams of those who gave the era its warmth and vitality.

metas.name: The Act of Killing
metas.description:
Impunity takes the form of performance. Indonesian mass killers, never punished and locally celebrated, gleefully re-stage their killings as Hollywood genres, until one man's body reacts before his conscience does.

A documentary which challenges former Indonesian death-squad leaders to reenact their mass-killings in whichever cinematic genres they wish, including classic Hollywood crime scenarios and lavish musical numbers.

metas.name: Grey Gardens
metas.description:
A mother and daughter live fused together in a decaying mansion. The Beales, relatives of Jackie Kennedy, singing, bickering and feeding raccoons in the attic — performing for the camera and trapped with each other.

Meet a mother and daughter, high-society dropouts, reclusive cousins of Jackie O., managing to thrive together amid the decay and disorder of their East Hampton, NY, mansion, making for an eerily ramshackle echo of the American Ca...

metas.name: Harlan County, USA
metas.description:
The strike is filmed from inside the picket line. Kentucky coal miners, their wives taking over the fight, company gunmen driving past at night — filmed as it happened, over years.

A heartbreaking record of the thirteen-month struggle between a community fighting to survive and a corporation dedicated to the bottom line.

metas.name: Flee
metas.description:
A hidden life story gets told for the first time. An animated documentary about a refugee from Afghanistan settled in Denmark, recounting flight, family separation and a secret he has kept from everyone.

A man looks back over his life as he grapples with a painful secret he has kept hidden for 20 years, one that threatens to derail the life he has built for himself and his soon to be husband.

metas.name: Stop Making Sense
metas.description:
This is a band building joy in real time. A Talking Heads concert that starts with David Byrne alone with a boombox and adds one musician per song until the stage is full — and his suit keeps getting bigger.

A live performance of the band Talking Heads shot over the course of three nights at Hollywood's Pantages Theater in December of 1983 and featuring their most memorable songs.

metas.name: Amazing Grace
metas.description:
Aretha Franklin's singing here is spiritual labour. She records a live gospel album in a Los Angeles church in 1972, over two nights, in a performance that visibly costs her something.

A documentary presenting Aretha Franklin with choir at the New Bethel Baptist Church in Watts, Los Angeles in January 1972.

metas.name: Summer of Soul
metas.description:
A community's archive sat in a basement for 50 years. What it held was the 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival — Stevie Wonder, Nina Simone, Mahalia Jackson, Sly Stone — in footage almost nobody saw.

Documentary about the legendary 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival which celebrated African-American music and culture and promoted Black pride and unity.

metas.name: The Last Waltz
metas.description:
A musical era ends on stage here, politely. The Band's farewell concert with everyone they came up with as guests, and backstage interviews with men who sound relieved and bereaved at once.

A film account and presentation of the final concert of The Band.

metas.name: Buena Vista Social Club
metas.description:
Elderly Cuban son musicians — some retired to shining shoes — are found again, recording and touring after years away; the pleasure is in their faces and Havana's streets.

A group of elder forgotten Cuban music legends emerge from obscurity when an American producer reunites them in Havana, leading to spectacular performances that reignite their musical legacy.

metas.name: 20 Feet from Stardom
metas.description:
The voices you know best belong to people you can't name. Backup singers for the Stones, Springsteen and Sting — huge talent, a career spent three steps behind someone else.

Backup singers live in a world that lies just beyond the spotlight. Their voices bring harmony to the biggest bands in popular music, but we've had no idea who these singers are or what lives they lead, until now.

metas.name: Microcosmos
metas.description:
At insect scale, a meadow becomes an alien world. One day in a French field, almost no narration: snails mating, a dung beetle rolling its ball uphill, rain arriving like artillery.

A documentary on insect life in meadows and ponds.

metas.name: Koyaanisqatsi
metas.description:
Civilisation itself becomes pattern. No dialogue or characters: time-lapse clouds, highways, factories, demolition and crowds cut to Philip Glass, until modern life starts to look like weather.

A collection of expertly photographed phenomena with no conventional plot. The footage focuses on the relationship between nature, humanity, and technology.

metas.name: Leviathan
metas.description:
Commercial fishing becomes a sensory ordeal. Cameras strapped to nets, chains, helmets and the hull of a North Atlantic trawler — fish heads, gulls, diesel, men half-asleep at 3 a.m., no explanation offered.

A documentary shot in the North Atlantic and focused on the commercial fishing industry.

metas.name: Senna
metas.description:
Speed, faith and charisma — entirely from archive. Ayrton Senna's career built only from period footage and voices — rivalry with Prost, Brazil on his helmet, in-car laps that feel like prayer at 300 km/h.

A documentary on Brazilian Formula One racing driver Ayrton Senna, who won the F1 world championship three times before his death at age 34.

metas.name: Free Solo
metas.description:
Alex Honnold's relationship to fear is simply different from yours. He prepares to climb El Capitan without ropes while the filmmakers — his friends — argue on camera about whether filming changes the odds.

Alex Honnold faces the biggest challenge of his career, climbing El Capitan in Yosemite National Park. He pursues it Free Solo, which means climbing without a rope and alone.

metas.name: When We Were Kings
metas.description:
Ali appears here as a political and verbal artist at his peak. The Rumble in the Jungle, Zaire 1974: training footage, a music festival, Mobutu's stadium, and Ali talking everyone, including himself, into belief.

Boxing documentary on the 1974 world heavyweight championship bout between defending champion, George Foreman, and the underdog challenger, Muhammad Ali.

metas.name: Jiro Dreams of Sushi
metas.description:
Mastery is repetition across a lifetime. An 85-year-old with a tiny Tokyo subway sushi counter and three Michelin stars, sons waiting to inherit, and a standard of 'delicious' he says he still hasn't reached.

A documentary on 85-year-old sushi master Jiro Ono, his renowned Tokyo restaurant, and his relationship with his son and eventual heir, Yoshikazu.

metas.name: Man with a Movie Camera
metas.description:
A city invents cinema while cinema invents the city. A Soviet day from waking to work to leisure, no story, and editing tricks in every minute that films still use — nearly a century old and showing off.

A man travels around a city with a camera slung over his shoulder, documenting urban life with dazzling invention.

metas.name: Sans Soleil
metas.description:
Memory is footage you keep re-narrating. A woman reads a travelling cameraman's letters over images of Tokyo, Guinea-Bissau, Iceland and San Francisco, until a travel film becomes a film about how a mind stores the world.

A woman narrates the contemplative writings of a seasoned world traveler, focusing on contemporary Japan.

metas.name: Los Angeles Plays Itself
metas.description:
A city is seen through the lies movies told about it. A video essay built entirely from clips — how Los Angeles is used as backdrop, villain and stand-in for everywhere else — narrated by a resident who loves it and resents all of it.

A documentary on how Los Angeles has been used and depicted in the movies.

metas.name: News from Home
metas.description:
Emigration is long shots and your mother's voice. New York — subways, diners, empty streets — while her mother's letters from Brussels, full of family news and worry, are read over it; homesickness with the geography reversed.

Impersonal and beautiful images of Akerman's life in New York are combined with letters from her loving but manipulative mother, read by Akerman herself.

metas.name: Stories We Tell
metas.description:
A family's central story turns out to have an author problem. Sarah Polley interviews her own family about her late mother; the accounts agree on the love and diverge on everything else, then the film shows you its own construction.

A film that excavates layers of myth and memory to find the elusive truth at the core of a family of storytellers.

metas.name: Honeyland
metas.description:
One woman's beehives hold a whole economy. A Macedonian beekeeper lives by one rule — take half the honey, leave half — until new neighbours arrive who take everything. A documentary that plays like an unscripted parable.

The last female bee-hunter in Europe must save the bees and return the natural balance in Honeyland, when a family of nomadic beekeepers invade her land and threaten her livelihood.

metas.name: Night and Fog
metas.description:
The Holocaust is approached through the quiet, empty camps a decade later rather than through footage of the killing itself: grass growing over atrocity, and how quickly a society decides to move on. Resnais' 32-minute essay remains documentary's foundational act of memory.

The history of Nazi Germany's death camps of the Final Solution and the hellish world of dehumanization and death contained inside.

metas.name: Chronicle of a Summer
metas.description:
This is the moment documentary stopped pretending the camera wasn't in the room. Rouch and Morin ask Parisians 'Are you happy?', then film themselves arguing over whether the answers were real — cinéma vérité examining its own honesty.

A documentary about the everyday lives of ordinary Parisians, done in the style of cinéma vérité.

metas.name: Titicut Follies
metas.description:
What an institution does to people when nobody outside is watching is on full display here. Wiseman inside a Massachusetts asylum for the criminally insane: no narration, no interviews, no mercy — a film banned for decades for what it showed.

Documentary filmmaker Frederick Wiseman takes us inside the Massachusetts Correctional Institution Bridgewater, where people stay trapped in their madness.

metas.name: Salesman
metas.director: Albert Maysles, David Maysles, Charlotte Zwerin
metas.description:
One rejected doorstep at a time, a man's self-belief runs out. The Maysles brothers follow a Bible salesman through Boston and Florida as his pitch slowly stops working and the road stops feeling like hope.

Four dogged door-to-door Bible salesmen travel from Boston to Florida on a seemingly futile quest to sell luxury editions of the Good Book to working-class Catholics.

metas.name: Gimme Shelter
metas.director: Albert Maysles, David Maysles, Charlotte Zwerin
metas.description:
The 1960s dream curdles in a single precise frame: Altamont, a fan stabbed to death in front of the stage, and the Rolling Stones afterwards watching the footage of it, not knowing what to say.

When three hundred thousand members of the Love Generation collided with a few dozen Hells Angels at San Francisco's Altamont Speedway, the bloody slash that transformed a decade's dreams into disillusionment was immortalized on t...

metas.name: Hearts and Minds
metas.description:
A country talks itself into a war here, and then can't talk itself out of the damage. Vietnam told by everyone it passed through — generals, pilots, Vietnamese villagers, American POWs and grieving parents.

A startling and courageous landmark documentary that unflinchingly confronted the United States' involvement in Vietnam at the height of the controversy that surrounded it.

metas.name: Burden of Dreams
metas.description:
Obsession becomes indistinguishable from the thing it depicts. Les Blank films Werner Herzog dragging a steamship over an Amazonian mountain to make Fitzcarraldo, losing his mind in exactly the way his character does.

A documentary following German auteur Werner Herzog as he deals with difficult actors, bad weather and getting a boat over a mountain, all in an effort to make his film Fitzcarraldo (1982).

metas.name: Shoah
metas.description:
Memory itself serves as the evidence. Nine and a half hours with not one frame of archival footage — only survivors, bystanders and perpetrators talking in the present tense, in the places where it happened. It makes extraordinary demands of its viewer.

Claude Lanzmann's epic documentary recounts the story of the Holocaust through interviews with witnesses - perpetrators as well as survivors.

metas.name: The Thin Blue Line
metas.description:
'Eyewitness truth' turns out to be mostly people confidently describing things that never happened. Errol Morris reconstructs a policeman's murder through conflicting accounts and stylised re-enactments — and the film's evidence helped free the man convicted of it.

A film that successfully argued that a man was wrongly convicted for murder by a corrupt justice system in Dallas County, Texas.

metas.name: Crumb
metas.description:
One brutal upbringing produces, in turn, a famous artist, a broken man, and something in between. Cartoonist R. Crumb and his two brothers, all shaped by one brutal household, in Terry Zwigoff's unsparing family portrait.

An intimate portrait of controversial cartoonist Robert Crumb and his traumatized family.

metas.name: American Movie
metas.description:
Delusion and genuine talent live in the same person here. Mark Borchardt, a Wisconsin sanitation worker with debts and a drinking problem, tries to finish a horror short to fund his dream feature — very funny until, suddenly, it isn't.

Aspiring filmmaker Mark Borchardt attempts to finance his dream project by finally completing Coven (1997), a micro-budget horror film he abandoned years before.

metas.name: The Gleaners and I
metas.description:
Resourcefulness becomes a whole philosophy of life, at the gentlest possible intensity. Agnès Varda follows people who live off what's left behind — fields, markets, bins — and turns her little digital camera on her own ageing hands.

Varda films and interviews gleaners in France in all forms, from those picking fields after the harvest to those scouring the dumpsters of Paris.

metas.name: Capturing the Friedmans
metas.description:
A family performs normality for a camera while everything underneath it collapses. A family accused of horrific crimes, told largely through their own compulsive home videos, which keep contradicting the legal case and each other.

Follows the Friedmans, a seemingly typical, upper-middle-class Jewish family whose world is instantly transformed when the father and his youngest son are arrested and charged with shocking and horrible crimes.

metas.name: The Fog of War
metas.description:
A brilliant man sits half-confessing to catastrophe. Robert McNamara, architect of Vietnam escalation, now in his eighties, lays out eleven lessons from his life in power — you decide whether the other half is honesty or self-defence.

The story of America as seen through the eyes of the former Secretary of Defense under President John F. Kennedy and President Lyndon B. Johnson, Robert McNamara.

metas.name: Grizzly Man
metas.description:
Nature never agreed to the story Timothy Treadwell kept narrating himself into. Herzog assembles Timothy Treadwell's own footage: thirteen summers living among Alaskan bears he insisted loved him, before one of them killed him.

A devastating and heart-rending take on grizzly bear activists Timothy Treadwell and Amie Huguenard, who were killed in October of 2003 while living among grizzly bears in Alaska.

metas.name: Dear Zachary: A Letter to a Son About His Father
metas.description:
Grief and legal-system failure are rendered with unmatched force. It begins as a film for a baby about the father he'll never meet, murdered before he was born — then the case takes a turn mid-production that is almost unbearable.

A filmmaker decides to memorialize a murdered friend when his friend's ex-girlfriend announces she is expecting his son.

metas.name: Man on Wire
metas.description:
The daring here is pure, pointless and joyful — a crime with no victim and no motive except beauty. Philippe Petit's 1974 tightrope walk between the Twin Towers, told like a heist film by the crew who smuggled the rigging up.

A look at tightrope walker Philippe Petit's daring, but illegal, high-wire routine performed between New York City's World Trade Center's twin towers in 1974, what some consider, "the artistic crime of the century".

metas.name: Nostalgia for the Light
metas.description:
Two kinds of searching for the past happen in the same frame. In Chile's Atacama desert, astronomers scan the sky for the universe's origins while women sift the same soil for the bones of Pinochet's disappeared.

A documentary about two different searches conducted in the Chilean Atacama Desert: one by astronomers looking for answers about the history of the cosmos, and one by women looking for the remains of loved ones killed by Pinochet'...

metas.name: The Imposter
metas.description:
People will go remarkably far to believe a story they want to be true. A missing Texas teenager 'returns' three years later, older and with a French accent — and his family accepts him. The man himself explains exactly how he did it.

A documentary centered on a young man in Spain who claims to a grieving Texas family that he is their 16-year-old son who has been missing for 3 years.

metas.name: Citizenfour
metas.description:
History happens at the speed of a man checking over his shoulder. Laura Poitras was already filming when Edward Snowden contacted her, so the leak of the century unfolds in a Hong Kong hotel room in real time.

A documentarian and a reporter travel to Hong Kong for the first of many meetings with Edward Snowden.

metas.name: Amy
metas.description:
The machinery of fame eats a person whose talent is right there on screen the whole time. Amy Winehouse's rise and destruction assembled from home video, voicemails and the tabloid footage that hunted her.

Archival footage and personal testimonials present an intimate portrait of the life and career of British singer/songwriter Amy Winehouse.

metas.name: Fire at Sea
metas.description:
Life goes on with surreal normality right next door to catastrophe. Lampedusa, where Europe's refugee crisis washes ashore, filmed alongside the utterly ordinary life of a local boy slingshotting cacti and listening to the radio.

Capturing life on the Italian island of Lampedusa, a frontline in the European migrant crisis.

metas.name: I Am Not Your Negro
metas.description:
Baldwin was a writer so precise that footage from decades after his death still fits his sentences. James Baldwin's unfinished manuscript on the murders of Medgar Evers, Malcolm X and Martin Luther King, read over a century of American images.

Writer James Baldwin tells the story of race in modern America with his unfinished novel, Remember This House.

metas.name: O.J.: Made in America
metas.description:
A whole country's contradictions run through one man's story. Nearly eight hours, and not really about a murder trial: Los Angeles, race, celebrity and policing across fifty years, with Simpson as the thread running through all of it.

A chronicle of the rise and fall of O.J. Simpson, whose high-profile murder trial exposed the extent of American racial tensions, revealing a fractured and divided nation.

metas.name: Faces Places
metas.description:
Art serves here as an excuse to pay attention to people, at the lightest and warmest of registers. Varda, 88 and going blind, tours rural France with photographer JR, pasting giant portraits of villagers onto their own villages.

Director Agnes Varda and photographer/muralist J.R. journey through rural France and form an unlikely friendship.

metas.name: Minding the Gap
metas.description:
The moment comes when a documentarian has to point the camera at himself. Bing Liu films his skateboarder friends in their rust-belt hometown over years, then slowly realises the film is about the violence they all grew up in — including his own.

Filmmaker Bing Liu searches for correlations between his skateboarder friends' turbulent upbringings and the complexities of modern masculinity.

metas.name: Apollo 11
metas.description:
The Moon landing unfolds in sheer procedural calm. Rebuilt entirely from restored 70mm footage and audio — no narration, no talking heads — just thousands of people doing small jobs correctly until a man is standing on the Moon.

A look at the Apollo 11 mission to land on the moon led by commander Neil Armstrong and pilots Buzz Aldrin and Mike Collins.

metas.name: For Sama
metas.description:
War is filmed from inside a family instead of inside a news report. Waad Al-Kateab films five years of the siege of Aleppo as a letter to her baby daughter, explaining why they stayed.

An intimate and epic journey into a young woman's experience of war during the revolution in Aleppo, Syria.

metas.name: Collective
metas.description:
Corruption gets dismantled in real time, and it plays like a thriller. After a Bucharest nightclub fire, burn victims start dying of infections in Romanian hospitals — and a sports newspaper, of all things, uncovers why.

Director Alexander Nanau follows a crack team of investigators at the Romanian newspaper Gazeta Sporturilor as they try to uncover a vast health-care fraud that enriched moguls and politicians and led to the deaths of innocent cit...

metas.name: Dick Johnson Is Dead
metas.description:
Dying gets approached with slapstick, tenderness and total honesty at once. Kirsten Johnson stages elaborate fake deaths for her psychiatrist father, who has dementia, so the two of them can rehearse losing each other.

A daughter helps her father prepare for the end of his life.

metas.name: Fire of Love
metas.description:
This is a love story where the third party is the Earth itself. Volcanologists Katia and Maurice Krafft filmed each other at the edge of eruptions for twenty years, knowing the work would probably kill them. It did, together, in 1991.

Intrepid scientists and lovers Katia and Maurice Krafft died in a volcanic explosion doing the very thing that brought them together: unraveling the mysteries of volcanoes by capturing the most explosive imagery ever recorded.

metas.name: 20 Days in Mariupol
metas.description:
The 2022 siege of Mariupol is shown as the people inside it actually experienced its first twenty days. AP journalists trapped in the city keep filming because getting the footage out is the only thing that makes staying mean anything.

An AP team of Ukrainian journalists trapped in the besieged city of Mariupol struggle to continue their work documenting atrocities of the Russian invasion.

metas.name: The Emperor's Naked Army Marches On
metas.description:
One man's war never ended: veteran Kenzo Okuzaki tours Japan forcing his former officers to answer on camera for executions and cannibalism in New Guinea, while director Kazuo Hara's crew effectively enlists in his campaign.

Kenzo Okuzaki, a 62-year-old anarchist veteran of the New Guinea campaign in World War II, sets out to conduct interviews with survivors and relatives to find the truth behind atrocities committed by Japanese military, in particular the unexplained killing of two Japanese privates in his unit.

metas.name: Extreme Private Eros: Love Song 1974
metas.description:
A filmmaker turns his merciless method on himself: Hara follows his ex-wife, radical feminist Miyuki Takeda, through lovers, communes and an unassisted birth, while his new partner records the sound — intimacy documented past every comfortable limit.

In this uncomfortably intimate film, documentary filmmaker Kazuo Hara visits his ex-girlfriend Miyuki and records her new relationships.

metas.name: Goodbye CP
metas.description:
The subjects seize the documentary itself: activists with cerebral palsy refuse every framing offered them, demanding to be looked at directly and confronting Hara's camera about what it wants from them.

An intimate documentary about a group of people with cerebral palsy in Japan that confronts our preconceptions and prejudices about who they are, what they feel, and how they view their lives.

metas.name: A Man Vanishes
metas.description:
A documentary dissolves into fiction: Imamura investigates a missing salesman, but the fiancée and the lead actress fall for each other, and he pulls the set apart on camera to admit the investigation has become something else.

A Man Vanishes examines the concept of Johatsu, tackling the phenomenon of people missing in Japan over the years. It picks one such person from the list, someone who had seemed to disappear from the face of the earth due to embezzlement from his company, and the filmmakers begin an investigative documentary into the reasons behind and attempt at tracking him down.

metas.name: A
metas.description:
Inside a demonised group, everyday life is startlingly banal: Mori films young Aum Shinrikyo believers doing chores after the sarin attack, sincere and confused, while the media siege outside performs its own hysteria.

Aum Shinrikyo, the Buddhist sect led by Shoko Asahara and responsible for the 1995 Sarin gas attack on a Tokyo subway, becomes the subject of this documentary.

metas.name: Minamata: The Victims and Their World
metas.description:
Resistance becomes a way of life: Tsuchimoto lives with Minamata's mercury-poisoned fishing families as they confront the Chisso corporation, sit in at shareholder meetings and refuse, for years, to go away.

The first in a series of independent documentaries that Tsuchimoto made of the mercury poisoning incident in Minamata, Japan.

metas.name: The Look of Silence
metas.description:
Confrontation is inverted: Adi, whose brother was murdered in Indonesia's 1965 purges, visits the killers under cover of eye exams and asks about the killings to their faces — no shouting, only unbearable quiet where they still hold power.

A family that survived the genocide in Indonesia confronts the men who killed one of their brothers.

metas.name: S-21: The Khmer Rouge Killing Machine
metas.description:
Atrocity is recalled as office procedure: survivor Vann Nath brings former Tuol Sleng guards back into the prison, where they re-enact their daily routines of shackling and paperwork and find nothing dramatic in their own memories.

A unique documentary on the notorious S-21 prison, today the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, with testimony by the only surviving prisoners and former Khmer Rouge guards.

metas.name: Symbiopsychotaxiplasm: Take One
metas.description:
A production seizes itself: Greaves films actors rehearsing a breakup while his crew, instructed to film everything, records its own growing revolt against him — and the revolt becomes the film, decades before the form existed.

Filmmaker William Greaves auditioned acting students for a fictional drama, while simultaneously shooting the behind-the-scenes drama taking place.

metas.name: Portrait of Jason
metas.description:
There comes a point where performance stops protecting a man: hustler and would-be cabaret act Jason Holliday performs his life all night for Shirley Clarke's provoking camera, until the act slowly, visibly cracks.

Black gay prostitute Jason Holliday is rigorously interviewed on his story and character, revealing nuanced truths about life and art.

metas.name: Warrendale
metas.description:
Institutional care runs out of composure: King's cameras live inside a Toronto home for emotionally disturbed children through tenderness, chaos and a staff member's sudden death — footage the CBC commissioned, then refused to air.

Chronicles 7-weeks in the lives of 12 emotionally disturbed children and their therapist's experimental method of treatment at the Toronto-area Warrendale facility.

metas.name: Land Without Bread
metas.description:
Documentary dishonesty is itself the subject: Buñuel's authoritative 'ethnography' of a destitute Spanish region stages scenes, lets animals die for the camera and lies in a straight-faced voiceover — in 1933, before the form had even settled.

A surrealistic documentary portrait of the region of Las Hurdes, a remote region of Spain where civilisation has barely developed, showing how the local peasants try to survive without even the most basic utilities and skills.

metas.name: Blood of the Beasts
metas.description:
Beneath a city's breakfast lies calm labour: Franju intercuts Paris waking at dawn with slaughterhouses already methodically killing horses and calves, workers chatting through the work, in twenty unflinching minutes.

An early example of ultra-realism, this movie contrasts the quiet, bucolic life in the outskirts of Paris with the harsh, gory conditions inside the nearby slaughterhouses. Describes the ...

metas.name: The Act of Seeing with One's Own Eyes
metas.description:
The camera is reduced to pure looking: Brakhage films autopsies in a Pittsburgh morgue silently and in close-up, with no commentary to hide behind, asking whether there is anything a camera should refuse to see.

At a morgue, forensic pathologists conduct autopsies of the corpses assigned. "S. Brakhage, entering, WITH HIS CAMERA, one of the forbidden, terrific locations of our culture, the autopsy room. It is a place wherein, inversely, life is cherished, for it exists to affirm that no one of us may die without our knowing exactly why. All of us, in the person of the coroner, must see that, for ourselves, with our own eyes. It is a room full of appalling particular intimacies, the last ditch of individuation. Here our vague nightmare of mortality acquires the names and faces of OTHERS. This last is a process that requires a WITNESS; and what 'idea' may finally have inserted itself into the sensible world we can still scarcely guess, for the CAMERA would seem the perfect Eidetic Witness, staring with perfect compassion where we can scarcely bear to glance." – Hollis Frampton

metas.name: On the Bowery
metas.description:
Neo-realist method eats its own ethics: Rogosin lived among New York's skid-row alcoholics, then had them play themselves in a story built from their lives, as the production's own drinking blurred every line.

A mix of documentary and scripted footage on the Bowery, New York City's skid row. Against a backdrop of men (and a few women) drinking in bars, talking and arguing, and sleeping on sidewalks, we have the story of Ray.

metas.name: The House Is Black
metas.description:
The refusal to look away turns tender: poet Forugh Farrokhzad films inside an Iranian leper colony — classes, a wedding, prayer — reading her own poetry over faces the world had agreed not to see.

Set in a leper colony in the north of Iran, The House is Black juxtaposes "ugliness," of which there is much in the world as stated in the opening scenes, with religion and gratitude.

metas.name: From a Night Porter's Point of View
metas.description:
An authoritarian personality describes itself as common sense: Kieślowski gives a factory night porter who adores rules, informers and surveillance enough rope to explain his whole worldview, delighted with himself throughout.

At the time of the Polish social regime, a security officer is promoted to work at a prison yard. Introducing concurrently with the narrator; he speaks of himself, his thoughts, his point of view.

metas.name: Aileen: Life and Death of a Serial Killer
metas.description:
A confrontational filmmaker finds his limit: Broomfield builds a real relationship with death-row killer Aileen Wuornos, testifies in her case, and films a final interview in which she is plainly no longer competent.

Nick Broomfield's second documentary about serial killer Aileen Wuornos, focusing on her mental state on death row.

metas.name: The Bridge
metas.description:
The complicity question arrives in its purest form: Steel filmed the Golden Gate Bridge for a year, recording suicides, without telling families what the footage was for — when the camera keeps rolling, what exactly is it doing?

Filmmakers use hidden cameras to capture the various suicide attempts at the Golden Gate Bridge - the world's most popular suicide destination. Interviews with the victims' loved ones describe their lives and mental health.

metas.name: Tickled
metas.description:
An investigation's subject fights back in real time: journalist David Farrier asks a cheerful question about 'competitive endurance tickling' videos and receives legal threats so disproportionate that following them becomes the film.

Journalist David Farrier stumbles upon a mysterious tickling competition online. As he delves deeper he comes up against fierce resistance, but that doesn't stop him getting to the bottom of a story stranger than fiction.

metas.name: Cameraperson
metas.description:
A career of looking is reckoned with: Kirsten Johnson cuts decades of outtakes from other people's difficult documentaries — Bosnia, Darfur, her own mother's decline — into a memoir about what pointing a camera at someone's worst day costs.

Exposing her role behind the camera, Kirsten Johnson reaches into the vast trove of footage she has shot over decades around the world. What emerges is a visually bold memoir and a revelatory interrogation of the power of the camera.

metas.name: Icarus
metas.description:
A documentary gets swallowed by its own story: Fogel films himself doping to expose how easy cheating is, but his Russian scientist accomplice sits at the centre of a state doping programme, and the film becomes his escape plan.

When Bryan sets out to uncover the truth about doping in sports, a chance meeting with a Russian scientist transforms his story from a personal experiment into a geopolitical thriller.

metas.name: Strong Island
metas.description:
Grief is conducted as cross-examination: Yance Ford investigates his brother's killing and the grand jury that declined to indict, addressing the camera directly and interrogating his own family's silence as hard as the legal system's.

When filmmaker Yance Ford investigates the 1992 murder of a young Black man, it becomes an achingly personal journey, since the victim, 24-year-old William Ford Jr., was the filmmaker's brother.

metas.name: The Battle of Chile
metas.description:
A revolution and its destruction were filmed by people unsure which they were recording: Guzmán's crew shoots Allende's final year in Chile's streets across three parts, as mass rallies and strikes give way to the coup arriving around the camera.

The chronicle of the political tension in Chile in 1973 and of the violent counter revolution against the democratically elected government of Salvador Allende.

metas.name: Baraka
metas.description:
Humanity becomes a planetary process. Shot in 70mm across 24 countries with no narration and no plot — prayer, factories, volcanoes, crowds moving like weather systems — beautiful and faintly horrifying in the same shots.

A collection of expertly photographed scenes of human life and religion.

metas.name: Winged Migration
metas.director: Jacques Perrin, Jacques Cluzaud, Michel Debats
metas.description:
Migration is shown from the bird's side of it. Cameras fly inside migrating flocks over years and continents, close enough to hear wingbeats — endurance as the most ordinary thing in the world.

Documentary on the migratory patterns of birds, shot over the course of three years on all seven continents.

metas.name: Gunda
metas.description:
A farm animal's inner life opens up simply because the film refuses to narrate it. Black and white, no music, no dialogue: a sow and her piglets, chickens and cows, at their own pace and eye level.

Documentary looks at the daily life of a pig and its farm animal companions: two cows and a one-legged chicken.

metas.name: All That Breathes
metas.description:
Two brothers in Delhi run a makeshift hospital for black kites falling out of a polluted sky, and caring for creatures everyone else steps over becomes a way of holding a world together while the city frays around them.

Amidst the darkening backdrop of Delhi's apocalyptic air and escalating violence, two brothers devote their lives to protect one casualty of the turbulent times: the bird known as the Black Kite.

metas.name: Chasing Ice
metas.description:
Climate change becomes visible at human time-scale here, no argument required. Time-lapse cameras planted on glaciers play back years of retreat in seconds — including a calving event the size of a city district, caught by chance.

Follow National Geographic photographer James Balog across the Arctic as he deploys time-lapse cameras designed for one purpose: to capture a multi-year record of the world's changing glaciers.

metas.name: The Salt of the Earth
metas.description:
This is what a lifetime of looking at suffering does to a person, and one answer to it. Photographer Sebastião Salgado walks through forty years of famine, war and exodus in his own images, then turns to restoring a dead forest — and it works.

The life and work of photographer Sebastião Salgado, who has spent forty years documenting societies in hidden corners of the world.

metas.name: Particle Fever
metas.description:
Big science's actual emotional texture runs through this film: boredom, terror, and a party when the bump appears in the data. The Large Hadron Collider's first runs filmed from inside the collaboration, theorists not knowing if thirty years of work is about to collapse.

As the Large Hadron Collider is about to be launched for the first time, physicists are on the cusp of the greatest scientific discovery of all time -- or perhaps their greatest failure.

metas.name: The Farthest
metas.description:
At the heart of this film is the most optimistic object our species has ever made, and the scientists ageing alongside it. The Voyager probes, told by the people who built them, carrying a golden record of human greetings out of the solar system.

It is one of humankind's greatest achievements. More than 12 billion miles away a tiny spaceship is leaving our Solar System and entering the void of deep space - the first human-made object ever to do so.

metas.name: Good Night Oppy
metas.description:
The engineers here grieve a machine — completely sincerely, and they earn it. Mars rover Opportunity, built for 90 days, worked for 15 years; the JPL team's attachment stops being a joke about anthropomorphism around year ten.

The film follows Opportunity, the Mars Exploration Rover affectionately dubbed Oppy by her creators and scientists at NASA. Oppy was originally expected to live for only 90 days but she ultimately explored Mars for nearly 15 years.

metas.name: AlphaGo
metas.description:
This film sits at the exact historical moment a machine did something its makers couldn't explain. DeepMind's system against Lee Sedol in Seoul, filmed in both camps; Move 37 lands and the human experts go quiet.

Google's DeepMind has developed a program for playing the 3000 year old game Go using AI. They test AlphaGo on the European champion, then March 9-15, 2016, on the top player, Lee Sedol, in a best of 5 tournament in Seoul.

metas.name: Lo and Behold: Reveries of the Connected World
metas.description:
Herzog treats the internet as something stranger and more fragile than either its utopians or critics describe. He wanders its birthplace, a monastery of monks with smartphones, a family hounded by trolls, and asks if the network dreams of itself.

Werner Herzog's exploration of the Internet and the connected world.

metas.name: The Atomic Cafe
metas.director: Jayne Loader, Kevin Rafferty, Pierce Rafferty
metas.description:
A state lies to its citizens here in its own cheerful voice. Nothing but 1940s–50s American government films, ads and newsreels about the bomb, cut together with no narration: duck and cover, soldiers reassured about fallout.

Disturbing collection of 1940s and 1950s United States government-issued propaganda films designed to reassure Americans that the atomic bomb was not a threat to their safety.

metas.name: They Shall Not Grow Old
metas.description:
Suddenly the trenches are populated by recognisable young men instead of ghosts. Peter Jackson restores jerky silent WWI footage to correct speed, colourises it, and adds voices reconstructed from veterans' interviews and lip-reading.

A documentary about World War I with never-before-seen footage to commemorate the centennial of the end of the war.

metas.name: A Film Unfinished
metas.description:
A fabricated archive keeps passing as truth until someone watches it slowly enough. A Nazi propaganda film shot in the Warsaw Ghetto is taken apart shot by shot, including outtakes where the staging shows.

A film about an unfinished film which portrays the people behind and before the camera in the Warsaw Ghetto, exposing the extent of the cinematic manipulation forever changing the way we look at historic images.

metas.name: Winter on Fire: Ukraine's Fight for Freedom
metas.description:
A protest becomes a revolution in real time in this film, and it shows what that costs the people who refuse to leave. Kyiv's Euromaidan over 93 days, from student demonstration to a government shooting its own citizens, filmed inside the square.

A documentary on the unrest in Ukraine during 2013 and 2014, as student demonstrations supporting European integration grew into a violent revolution calling for the resignation of President Viktor F. Yanukovich.

metas.name: 13th
metas.description:
DuVernay works here at the essay-documentary's maximum force — a thesis you can feel being assembled. One chain is built from the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause through convict leasing, Jim Crow and the war on drugs to mass incarceration.

An in-depth look at the prison system in the United States and how it reveals the nation's history of racial inequality.

metas.name: Inside Job
metas.description:
Elite impunity lives in this film as a tone of voice. The 2008 financial crisis explained with unusual clarity and barely suppressed fury, including interviews where the architects keep incriminating themselves with total calm.

Takes a closer look at what brought about the 2008 financial meltdown.

metas.name: Paradise Lost: The Child Murders at Robin Hood Hills
metas.description:
This Satanic-panic prosecution is filmed from the inside, and the film itself became evidence in the decades-long fight over the case. Three Arkansas teenagers convicted of murder largely for liking Metallica and black clothes, filmed through the trial with access to every family.

A horrific triple child murder leads to an indictment and trial of three nonconformist boys based on questionable evidence.

metas.name: Searching for Sugar Man
metas.description:
Fame exists in full, in a place the famous person never knew about. Detroit singer Rodriguez, a flop at home in the 1970s and rumoured dead, was bigger than Elvis in apartheid South Africa. Sheer joy, start to finish.

Two South Africans set out to discover what happened to their unlikely musical hero, the mysterious 1970s rock n roller, Rodriguez.
